summary: Iter17 backend tests for expense-categories (natures de depense) + invoice account derivation + distribution-keys usage/force-detach + auto-entry manual edit policy. 19/19 PASS. iter16 regression 16/16 PASS. All 14 features from the request validated end-to-end against the live preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/expense_categories.py: PUT update_category does NOT change copropriete_id even when payload provides a different one because $set uses data.model_dump() but 1:1 conflict check uses data.copropriete_id or existing.copropriete_id. If a category is moved across ACPs via PUT, the 1:1 check may pass while the persisted copropriete_id is updated to a value the conflict check did not actually test against. Mitigation: ignore copropriete_id on PUT (immutable), or re-validate against the NEW copropriete_id explicitly.

routes/expense_categories.py: list_categories enriches account_name only for PCMNs in the same copropriete_id when one is provided; otherwise the PCMN lookup uses pq without copropriete_id and may match the wrong ACP's account name in multi-ACP setups (account numbers can repeat per ACP). Low impact today (1 ACP) but will surface when a 2nd ACP is added.

routes/invoices.py: update_invoice does NOT clear distribution_lines when distribution_key_id is changed via PUT; the recomputed lines should be saved (POST does compute them). Today PUT only persists distribution_key_id without recomputing distribution_lines. Recommend mirroring the POST logic in PUT for consistency.

routes/invoices.py: PUT /distribution-keys/{id}?force=true performs the update BEFORE detaching invoices. If detach succeeds but invoice update_many fails, the key is already renamed/restructured. Recommend wrapping detach+update in a transaction (or detach first then update) so partial failures don't leave an inconsistent state.

routes/accounting.py: PUT entry marks manually_edited only when existing.auto_generated is True. If a user reverts the entry to its original lines, the manually_edited flag remains True forever, allowing later DELETE. That's actually fine policy-wise but is asymmetric with the 'protect auto entries' intent — consider documenting that manual edit is a one-way detach from auto-regen lifecycle.

auto_entries._delete_auto_entries: when an invoice's source is updated, the new auto entry is inserted alongside the kept manually_edited one => the journal now contains TWO entries for the same source (one manual+stale, one auto+fresh). Balance reports will double-count this invoice. This is the behavior asserted by test_update_source_skips_manually_edited and may be the desired protection, but the main agent should confirm semantics: typically a manually_edited entry should DETACH from source (clear source_id) so generate_purchase_entry doesn't create a duplicate.
